changes_made.reason: AC-level environment defect, not an artifact defect and not builder-fixable. The verifier (run ab6abd6d, tip 38770e37) measured ac1 deterministic 2/2 rc=1 with failure_type=test_env at the byte-identity leg cmp -s security/gitleaks-report.json "$r1". Root cause (verifier-proven and independently reproduced in this re_groom): core.autocrlf=true is set at REPO-LOCAL level, so a fresh checkout converts the committed 3-byte LF blob fe51488c ("[]\n") into a 4-byte CRLF working-tree file ("[]\r\n"), while gitleaks always writes LF; the pinned cmp therefore compares the CRLF-mangled working-tree copy against fresh LF tool output and is UNSATISFIABLE in any fresh autocrlf=true checkout. No builder-side fix exists: git add normalizes CRLF->LF under autocrlf=true (both LF- and CRLF-authored content hashes to blob fe51488c), the card pins blob == fe51488c, and .gitattributes / repo config are outside this card (3 files pinned, .gitignore byte-frozen). The builder only passed because its worktree still held the tool-written LF file that was never re-checked-out - a state unreproducible from a fresh checkout. Correction (verifier-recommended option A, t36 precedent): CR-normalize the committed-report side before cmp, cmp -s <(tr -d "\r" < security/gitleaks-report.json) "$r1" - matching the established t36 treatment where tr -d CR reproduces pinned hashes under autocrlf. Semantics preserved: the gate is still a strict byte-equality check against the committed artifact (a real content drift such as a whitespace-different zero-findings payload still fails rc=1, measured) and the zero-leak BLOCKING invariant remains enforced by the untouched node zero-findings parse; a genuine leak (non-empty array) still blocks the card before any cmp runs.

residual_risks: The CR-normalization is a per-card side-step, not a repo-level cure: any FUTURE card that byte-compares a committed artifact against freshly generated tool output under core.autocrlf=true hits the same unsatisfiable cmp. Option B (repo-level .gitattributes -text rule for security report artifacts) or C (core.autocrlf=false) remains the standing alternative and is the orchestrator call; this re_groom deliberately touched no repo config and added no files (the card pins 3 files and freezes .gitignore).

Correctness against future CRLF-authored report content: the CR-normalization side-step stays correct, because git add normalizes CRLF->LF under autocrlf=true, so CRLF-authored and LF-authored content of the same payload both hash to the same committed blob and both CR-normalize to the tool output. The gate cannot be satisfied by CRLF-padded CONTENT drift that changes the payload (negative control d2: a byte-different zero-findings payload still fails rc=1).

The gate now compares CR-STRIPPED committed content, so a hypothetical payload whose meaningful bytes include a literal CR would be normalized away. Unreachable here: gitleaks JSON output is LF-only and the artifact must additionally parse as a JSON array with zero findings.

The built-state hash is stale: the builder handoff records ac_hash b43c7024 while the card now pins d92c8462, so the orchestrator must route a Builder pass (fix_qa at 16.7 percent materiality, or fresh implement) that re-runs the six pinned commands and re-stamps the hash before verification.
